title: The Cunning Wolf
author: Ellen C. Babbitt
summary: 人装死想骗猎物，狼王抽走他的木棒，识破了把戏。
publicDomainBasis: Retold by Ellen C. Babbitt and published in 1922 by The Century Co. (pre-1923, public domain in the United States); Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: Once upon a time the people in a certain town went out into the woods for a holiday. They took baskets full of good things to eat. But when noontime came they ate all the meat they had brought with them, not leaving any for supper.
paragraphs.zh: 从前，某个镇上的人们到树林里去过节。他们带了几篮子好吃的东西。可到了中午，他们把带来的肉全吃光了，一点也没给晚饭留。

paragraphs.en: "I will get some fresh meat. We will make a fire here and roast it," said one of the men.
paragraphs.zh: “我去弄点鲜肉来。我们在这儿生火烤着吃。”其中一个人说。

paragraphs.en: So taking a club, he went to the lake where the animals came to drink. He lay down, club in hand, pretending to be dead.
paragraphs.zh: 于是他拿起一根木棒，来到动物们饮水的湖边，手里握着木棒躺下，装死。

paragraphs.en: When the animals came down to the lake they saw the man lying there and they watched him for some time.
paragraphs.zh: 动物们来到湖边，看见那人躺在那儿，便观察了他一阵。

paragraphs.en: "That man is playing a trick on us, I believe," said the King of the Wolves. "The rest of you stay here while I will see whether he is really dead, or whether he is pretending to be dead."
paragraphs.zh: “我相信那人在耍花招，”狼王说，“你们其余的都待在这儿，我去看看他是真死了，还是装死。”

paragraphs.en: Then the cunning King of the Wolves crept up to the man and slyly pulled at his club.
paragraphs.zh: 于是狡猾的狼王悄悄凑到那人身边，偷偷去拨他手里的木棒。

paragraphs.en: At once the man pulled back on his club.
paragraphs.zh: 那人立刻往回一拽木棒。

paragraphs.en: Then the King of the Wolves ran off saying: "If you had been dead, you would not have pulled back on your club when I tried to pull it away. I see your trick. You pretend you are dead so that you may kill one of us for your supper."
paragraphs.zh: 狼王转身就跑，说：“你要是真死了，我来抽木棒时你就不会往回拽。我看穿你的把戏了。你装死，是想打死我们中的一个当晚饭。”

paragraphs.en: The man jumped up and threw his club at the King of the Wolves. But he missed his aim. He looked for the other animals but there was not one in sight. They had all run away.
paragraphs.zh: 那人跳起来，把木棒朝狼王扔去，却没打中。他再找别的动物，一只也不见了。它们全都跑掉了。

paragraphs.en: Then the man went back to his friends, saying: "I tried to get fresh meat by playing a trick on the animals, but the cunning Wolf played a better trick on me, and I could not get one of them."
paragraphs.zh: 于是那人回到朋友们那里，说：“我想耍花招弄点鲜肉，可狡猾的狼耍了更高明的花招，我一只也没弄到。”
